_comment: The hardest boundary in the stack: this skill authors REQ-* intent and acceptance, while
spec-driven-development authors the Layer 1 plan, ADRs and slice artifacts from it. Hard
negatives therefore lean on Layer 1-4 vocabulary.

trigger.prompt: Write the REQ-* requirements baseline for the aws-deployment milestone
Produce INITIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md with EARS acceptance criteria and NFRs for this milestone
We need testable Given/When/Then acceptance and a milestone glossary before planning
Define the agent operational boundaries: always do, ask first, never do
Requirements changed after a handback — evolve the existing requirements baseline and keep the REQ ids stable
Extract scope, requirements and acceptance criteria from this PRD into our milestone requirements structure
Add a negative scenario and a response measure to each requirement before we freeze it
Draft our durable product vision and North Star statement
Sequence the remaining milestones on Now/Next/Later horizons
Produce the Layer 1 detailed planning and the milestone ADRs
Plan the first vertical slice: mini-spec, delivery stories and engineering tasks
Implement this slice and record its closeout with reproduce commands
Revalidate the roadmap now that the milestone shipped

behavior.prompt: Use the first Now milestone in docs/specs/ROADMAP.md and produce its INITIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md.
expected_behavior: Reads the milestone row in ROADMAP.md and the CAP-*/QA-* in PRODUCT_STATEMENT.md before drafting
Reads ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md and TECH_STACK.md for constraints without copying their content
Asks 3-7 clarifying questions, or records explicit assumptions when told to proceed
Writes the file at docs/specs/milestones/<slug>/ using the roadmap's exact slug
Gives every REQ-* a stable id, an upstream CAP-*/QA-* citation, BDD or EARS acceptance, and at least one negative scenario
Keeps every QA-*-realizing NFR's response measure
Records the adversarial critique pass and states the handoff to spec-driven-development

behavior.prompt: The Step 4a handback for slice 4 changed what REQ-006 has to guarantee. Update the requirements.
expected_behavior: Edits the existing file rather than recreating it
Preserves existing REQ-* ids; marks anything retired as superseded with a one-line reason
Re-checks the changed requirement's acceptance and any NFR response measure it realizes
Appends a Change log entry naming the triggering handback
Does not re-plan Layers 2-4, and re-states the handoff so SDD re-ingests the file

behavior.prompt: Which of our requirements for this milestone are not actually testable?
expected_behavior: Answers the question instead of rewriting the file
Names specific requirements whose acceptance is ambiguous or missing an error scenario
Flags NFRs with no response measure and requirements citing no CAP-*/QA-*
Suggests the concrete command or check that would prove each weak requirement
